text:
priya: Weird production hit: a customer reported dropped SSE events during long-lived streams. Console showed steady `bytes_in` but client missing every 60th event.

luis: Any pattern in sequence IDs or Last-Event-ID header?

priya: Yes. Client logs show they reconnect with Last-Event-ID=42 and receive events 43..100 but every 60th (i.e., 60, 120, 180) is missing. Server logs show we emitted them.

emma: Could the proxy be coalescing chunk boundaries and truncating the trailing "\n" that separates SSE events? If an event delimiter is lost, client may treat two events as one.

priya: I grabbed a tcpdump around the proxy. Snippet:```\n12:05:00.000 -> chunk: "data: {\"id\":59}\n\n"\n12:05:00.120 -> chunk: "data: {\"id\":60}\n"\n12:05:00.121 -> chunk: "data: {\"id\":61}\n\n"\n```\nSee how event 60 lacks the double-newline, ends with single `\n` (likely due to buffer flush). Client treats event 60 and 61 as one event body and discards one id.

luis: That fits. Our SSE framing relies on double-newline between events. Why would the proxy drop a `\n`? Maybe chunked-transfer encoding boundary + proxy rewrite?

emma: We recently enabled `proxy.chunk_coalesce=true` in EU to reduce small TCP writes. It coalesces adjacent small buffers and rewrites Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding heuristics. Bug: it sometimes merges but fails to append the extra `\n` separator when the writer ended with a single `\n` and next buffer starts with `data:` (missing the empty line).

priya: So coalesce reduced syscalls but broke logical event separators. Oof.

luis: Immediate mitigation: add a proxy rule to inject an extra `\n` whenever we detect `data:.*\ndata:` across buffer boundary. Cheap hack until fix.

emma: We should also add console telemetry: event-parse-errors and event-coalesce-mutations counts. Currently console only shows bytes and connection states, nothing about parse-level deltas.

priya: Agree. UX was confusing for support because `bytes_in` looked normal. If we expose `sse_event_boundary_mutations` per route and a small sample payload when a mutation occurs, that would speed triage.

luis: Risk: exposing samples might leak PII. Make sure sampled payloads are redacted or only capture meta like `id` and size.

emma: Also check canary flags: I think chunk_coalesce was rolled to 30% last week. Need to narrow to EU hosts only.

ops-bot: Canary rollback requested: proxy/coalesce -> rollback host group eu-1. Pending manual approval. Link: https://deploy.internal/redwood/rollbacks/9981

priya: For the long term: update our SSE library to emit explicit event separators (i.e., always write `\n\n` as an atomic write) and add a unit test that simulates TCP-level splits and proxy coalescing. Without atomic separator, any intermediary rewrite can change semantics.

luis: Good point. Also propose adding a parser at the edge that validates SSE framing on egress and increments a metric when it repairs a boundary. That gives us observability and lets the console graph it.

emma: Console work: add a small timeline per connection that marks "boundary repair" ticks. Operators can then correlate to coalesce toggle.

priya: I'll open three PRs: 1) quick proxy-rule inject for the canary rollback window, 2) SSE library atomic-writes + tests, 3) console telemetry + sample-safe capture.

luis: For the rollback, can we do a gradual shrink (30% -> 10% -> 0%) so we don't flip everything at once?

ops-bot: Rollback plan posted: gradual scale down 30% -> 10% (10m) -> 0% (10m). Manual confirm required at each step.

emma: Add runbook note: "If clients miss periodic events at regular intervals, check proxy.coalesce, inspect sse_event_boundary_mutations and sample histogram."

priya: Captured a couple more traces across regions and all show same boundary pattern. I'll paste PR links when ready.

luis: Thx. Low-severity but high-impact for streaming UX. Glad we caught it before more customers noticed. :heart:

ops-bot: Rollback step 1 executed: scale to 10% in eu-1. Monitoring for mutation count.

priya: Monitoring now. mutation_count dropped from ~18/min -> ~1/min on canary hosts. Good sign.

emma: Follow-up: add a unit test in proxy that simulates `write("data:...\n")` then `write("data:...")` and assert final buffer contains `data:...\n\n` between events. Prevent regressions.

priya: Will do. Will post PRs and runbook edits shortly.
